title: Platform, licensing, and releases
blurb: Tenants, roles, access keys, and how to read a release note without sanding off the dates.

lessons.title: The Admin application
lessons.summary: Admin is where employees, roles, login authenticators, and access keys are managed. The app selector is how you get there.
objectives: Open Admin on purpose
List what Admin owns
Leave ACD skills for the ACD application

sections.h: What the welcome page assigns to Admin
p: The users and security page says the Admin application manages general components of the system. The key areas it names are employees, tenant-level settings and security, storage options, and recordings. Security and data access are managed with roles, views, login authenticators, and access keys.

Creating an inbound skill is not an Admin task. Set Up Inbound Voice starts in the ACD application, under Contact Settings. If a runbook mixes those two apps, the buttons will not be where the runbook says.
Every employee must have a minimum of one role. A secondary role is allowed when a person needs one. Permissions on the role decide which features, data, and applications that person can open.
Getting Started uses the same employee object for an API user. You still create the profile in Admin. A back-end integration user should not receive a login authenticator.

lessons.title: Licenses the help pages actually name
lessons.summary: Some features say they need a license. This lab lists only licenses a cited page names, and it does not invent SKUs or prices.
objectives: Treat a license sentence as a gate
Name three licenses the pages state
Refuse a price that is not published here

figure.caption: A license gate in front of a feature

p: CRM Ticketing says the feature is available if you have a CRM Ticketing license. Migrated Calls refers to an Interactions Upload license and to Admin > Recording > Upload Migrated Interactions permissions. AutoSummary setup says you must work with your account representative and that AutoSummary must be enabled. To use it with MAX rather than an agent application, you also need a Copilot for Agents license.
Salesforce integration says you are billed for CRM integration based on the number of employees with the Agent Integrations attribute enabled. That is a billing sentence, not a public price list.

sections.h: What this lab will not add
p: Release notes say you may need to purchase a license or join a public preview to use some features. They do not publish a catalog of SKUs in the passages used here.
If a design names a SKU this lab has not cited, mark it unknown and ask the account representative. Do not copy a SKU from memory into a statement of work.

lessons.title: Roles and least privilege
lessons.summary: Permissions live on roles. An API user gets a unique role with only the permissions the integration uses. An access key inherits that power.
objectives: Put permissions on roles
Build a narrow role for a connector
Remember a key is as powerful as its user

p: Security settings that control what users can see and do are roles and permissions. Access to recordings, reports, interactions, dashboards, and admin tools is typically permission-based. An agent may see only their own interactions. A supervisor may see a team.
Getting Started's best practice for a back-end app is a unique role with the minimum permissions for the actions the app performs, and no login authenticator.

sections.h: The Avaya connector does it the same way
p: The Avaya CMS page tells you to create a role for the connector and an employee for the connector, then generate the access key on that employee. The legacy page warns that the key receives all permissions of the user who generates it. An administrator's key is an administrator's key.
If the secret is lost, you create a new one. The secret is shown so you can copy it, and you will not see it again later.

steps.label: New role
steps.detail: Name it for the connector. Enable only the service permissions.

steps.label: New employee
steps.detail: No extra features. Activate the account so the Access Keys tab exists.

steps.label: Generate
steps.detail: Copy the id and the secret immediately.

steps.label: Disable later
steps.detail: A disabled key's tokens stop at once and cannot be refreshed.

quiz.q: Best practice for an integration role?

A copy of the administrator role

quiz.q: What happens when an access key is disabled?

Nothing until the next major release
quiz.why: Manage Access Keys describes instant checks.

quiz.q: An agent viewing only their own interactions is an example of what?
quiz.why: The Admin page uses that example.

cards.back: The object that holds permissions.
A unique role limited to what the integration does.
Copy it then. A lost secret means a new key.
Existing tokens from that key stop.

lab.title: Draw the inheritance
lab.goal: Show why you never generate a connector key as yourself.
steps: Write your administrator role on the left and a connector role with two permissions on the right.
Generate an imaginary key under each.
Circle the administrator key and write 'this is an admin credential'.
Add the disable test: turn the key off and expect calls to fail at once.
lab.done: The picture argues against shared admin keys.

faults.title: Connector running as admin
faults.symptom: A compromised connector account can edit employees.
faults.cause: The key was generated on an administrator, which the legacy page tells you not to do.
faults.fix: Create a dedicated role and employee, generate a new key there, and disable the old key.

lessons.title: External identity providers
lessons.summary: Users can authenticate with an external IdP. Applications authenticate with access keys. The help page lists the OIDC endpoints you copy from the IdP, including end-session for single logout.
objectives: Separate user login from app login
Name the endpoints the page lists
Keep SAML support inside what a release note said

sections.h: What the external IdP page asks for
p: If you do not have a discovery document, the external IdP page tells you to enter Issuer, JsonWebKeySet, Authorization, Token, UserInfo, Revocation, and End Session endpoints. End Session is how a logout from CXone Mpower can also log the user out of the IdP, if you whitelist the sign-out redirect URI at the IdP.

The same page says users and applications authenticate in similar ways, with one difference: applications use an access key, and users use a username and password. Applications are not required to use a browser. They are often back-office jobs or virtual agents.

The French 25.4 release notes describe global authentication support for sign-in started at an external SAML 2.0 IdP, and they name Microsoft Entra ID and OneLogin among supported providers. That passage was retrieved in French.

Use the current English authentication page before you tell a customer a specific IdP is on the supported list. The endpoint list above is from the English external IdP page and does not depend on that translation.

lessons.title: Public Preview, formerly Controlled Release
lessons.summary: Starting with the 26.3 release, the Controlled Release program is named Public Preview. Features on a release page may still require that program or a license.
objectives: Use the new name
Not assume a listed feature is generally available
Re-read dates before a freeze

figure.caption: A feature can sit behind a program

p: The 26.3 release notes say that starting with that release, the NiCE CXone Controlled Release program is known as Public Preview. The change is reflected in the online help, the release notes, and other communications.
The same page says you may have to purchase a license or sign up for a public preview to use some features, and that you may receive features at different times in the cycle.

The 26.2 notes include a rename table. Examples recorded from that page: Digital Experience (DX) stays associated with Digital Experience, and CXone Mpower for Service Cloud Voice is listed as moving to Unified App for Salesforce Voice. Treat the table as a point-in-time rename list, and open the page before you correct a customer's old name.

Agent application names in current help include Agent Workspace (Agent), Agent Workspace (Embedded), Agent Workspace for Microsoft Teams, and Agent Workspace (Browser Extension). Older documents say MAX. Both appear in current pages, so do not pretend MAX has vanished.

lessons.title: Access keys are not passwords
lessons.summary: A person logs in with a password or an IdP. A back-end app sends an access key id and secret to the token endpoint. The global token URL comes from OpenID discovery, not from a guess.
objectives: Call discovery before the token URL
Map key id and secret onto the password grant
Plan refresh before expiry

p: Getting Started says a back-end app provides an access key id and secret. For client_secret_basic, you send a basic authorization header with the application's client id and secret, and a form body with grant_type password, username set to the access key id, and password set to the secret. client_secret_post puts the client id and secret in the body instead.

You learn the token URL from the discovery document. Global production discovery is https://cxone.niceincontact.com/.well-known/openid-configuration. The sample response on the page includes token_endpoint https://cxone.niceincontact.com/auth/token.

The page says the token response includes a TTL, and that you should plan to renew before 5 minutes of access token expiry. It also says expires_in may differ from one token to the next. The sample token body shows expires_in 3600. Treat 3600 as that sample, not a contract.
OpenID Connect, for a user-facing app, is a different flow: scope openid, response_type code, then an authorization code at the token endpoint. Do not paste the password grant into a browser login.

steps.label: GET openid-configuration
steps.detail: Use the issuer for the environment.

steps.label: POST token_endpoint
steps.detail: grant_type=password.

steps.label: Read expires_in
steps.detail: Renew before the last five minutes.

steps.label: Authorization Bearer
steps.detail: Then discover api_endpoint with tenantId.

quiz.q: In the password grant, what is the username?
quiz.why: Getting Started maps username to the access key id and password to the secret.

quiz.q: Where do you read the token URL?
choices: token_endpoint in the OpenID discovery document
quiz.why: Do not skip discovery.

quiz.q: Global production issuer?
quiz.why: FedRAMP is https://cxone-gov.niceincontact.com.

quiz.q: The renewal tip on the page is…
choices: Renew before 5 minutes of access-token expiry
quiz.why: expires_in is not guaranteed to stay at the sample value.

quiz.q: The sample expires_in on Getting Started is…
quiz.why: It is a sample. The page says each exchange can differ.

quiz.q: A user-facing app should use which OpenID values?
choices: grant_type password in the browser with the agent's password
quiz.why: Those are the only supported values the page names for that flow.

cards.back: Access key id, on the back-end password grant.
Access key secret. Not the employee's login password.
Taken from discovery. Sample: /auth/token on the global issuer.
Renew before that much life remains.

lab.title: Fill a token card
lab.goal: Use the sample values only as labels.
steps: Write the discovery URL for global production.
Write grant_type, username, and password with the field mapping, not with a real secret.
Add expires_in and the five-minute rule.
Add a second card for OIDC that says authorization code, not password.
lab.done: The two cards cannot be swapped by mistake.

faults.title: Agent password in the server
faults.symptom: A back-end job stores an agent's password and sends it as the OAuth password.
faults.cause: The password field on that grant is the access key secret. The employee for a back-end app has no login authenticator.
faults.fix: Create an access key on a least-privilege employee and rotate the leaked password.

lessons.title: Employee attributes that turn features on
lessons.summary: A role is not the only switch. Digital agents need the Digital Engagement attribute. Salesforce screen-pop needs Agent Integrations and Customer Card. Those attributes can also be how you are billed.
objectives: Find attributes on the employee
Name Digital Engagement
Name the two Salesforce attributes

p: Digital Channels says agents need a supported agent application, permissions for each channel, the Digital Engagement attribute on the employee profile, and assignment to the digital skills or routing queues for that channel. MAX supports the digital channels the page discusses. Agent Workspace support depends on the application, and the page tells you to check that application's details.
A skill assignment without the attribute is not the whole setup. The page lists both.

The Salesforce Agent Workspace page says to enable Customer Card so agents can see the customer card, and Agent Integrations so they can open Agent Workspace for Salesforce and see Salesforce records in the card. Billing follows the count of employees with Agent Integrations enabled.
The Salesforce org must be Lightning, and it must use console navigation. Standard navigation opens each record in a new browser tab.
